overview: The Modified Electronics Manufacturing Clusters (EMC 2.0) scheme is a government initiative under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) aimed at strengthening India's electronics manufacturing ecosystem by developing world-class infrastructure and common facilities in electronics manufacturing clusters. The scheme supports the creation of plug-and-play infrastructure, common facility centers, and other enabling infrastructure to attract investments in electronics manufacturing. It aims to enhance India's competitiveness in global electronics value chains and promote domestic value addition.
objectives: To create world-class infrastructure for electronics manufacturing
To provide plug-and-play facilities and common facility centers
To attract investments in electronics manufacturing sectors
To enhance domestic value addition in electronics manufacturing
To promote exports and reduce imports of electronic goods
To generate employment opportunities in the electronics sector
To promote innovation and R&D in electronics manufacturing
To support the development of semiconductor and display manufacturing ecosystems
eligibility: State Governments, Union Territory Administrations, and their agencies/organizations are eligible to apply for setting up Electronics Manufacturing Clusters (EMCs) under the scheme. Private entities can also participate as Special Purpose VGF (Viability Gap Funding) scheme. Private sector entities can participate through Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) in partnership with State Governments/UT Administrations. The scheme supports Greenfield and Brownfield projects for electronics manufacturing, including semiconductor and display fabrication units.
benefits: Financial support in the form of Viability Gap Funding (VGF) up to 50% of the project cost for Greenfield EMCs and 75% for Brownfield EMCs, with a ceiling of INR 500 crore per 100 acres of land. Additional support includes infrastructure development such as roads, water supply, power supply, effluent treatment plants, and common facility centers like testing labs, design centers, and skill development centers. The scheme also provides support for land acquisition, site development, and enabling infrastructure to create plug-and-play facilities for electronics manufacturers.
financial_support: The scheme provides Viability Gap Funding (VGF) as a capital subsidy: up to 50% of project cost for Greenfield Electronics Manufacturing Clusters (EMCs) and up to 75% for Brownfield EMCs, with a maximum ceiling of INR 500 crore per 100 acres of land. The financial support is disbursed in milestones linked to project milestones such as land acquisition, site development, and infrastructure creation. The funding is intended to cover infrastructure development including roads, water, power, effluent treatment, and common facility centers like testing labs, design centers, and skill development centers.
grant_amount_per_entity: INR 500 crore per 100 acres of land
application_process: 1. State Government/UT Administration or its agency identifies land and prepares a Detailed Project Report (DPR) for the Electronics Manufacturing Cluster (EMC). 2. The proposal is submitted to the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) through the State Government/UT Administration. 3. MeitY appraises the proposal through an Expert Committee or Project Appraisal Committee. 4. Upon approval, an In-Principle Approval (IPA) is issued. 5. The State Government/UT Administration acquires the land and begins site development. 6. Detailed Project Report (DPR) is submitted for final approval. 7. Upon final approval, the Viability Gap Funding (VGF) is released in milestones linked to project progress. 8. The State Government/UT Administration or its agency implements the project and develops the infrastructure. 9. The developed infrastructure is made available to electronics manufacturers on a plug-and-play basis.
required_documents: No Objection Certificates (NOCs) from relevant authorities
Details of Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) if applicable
Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with anchor tenants if any
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year subject to availability of funds and appraisal cycles.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)
caveats: Funding is subject to availability of funds under the scheme
Projects must comply with all statutory and regulatory clearances
Land must be free from encumbrances and litigation
The scheme supports only electronics manufacturing and related activities
Beneficiaries must comply with environmental and labor laws
Funding is released in milestones based on project progress verification
The scheme does not cover land cost, only infrastructure development
Private sector participation must be through a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV)
